title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
layout_note: Three columns, one per component, each under a full-width pill-shaped heading bar: a circular task curriculum on the left, a code listing in the centre, a skill list on the right. A bottom row holds the environment screenshot and a self-verification magnifier icon; arrows from the bottom row climb back up into all three columns, so the environment is the shared hub of three loops.
grouping: Column headings are rounded bars with pastel fills, one colour per component (lavender, light blue, pale yellow), and the arrows leaving or entering each column take a darker shade of the same hue (purple for curriculum, blue for retrieval, green for adding a skill, red for refinement). The skill library is a pale-yellow rounded panel; the code sits on a light-grey rounded panel with no outline. The curriculum has no container: its tasks float on white.
shapes_depth: Flat. Tasks in the curriculum are circular game screenshots with a lavender ring, joined by black curved arrows into an arc (the last step dashed). The generated program is shown as real monospace code with grey comments. Each skill is a row with a small item icon and a text label; newly learned skills are coloured blue or green. The environment is a game title-screen screenshot; self-verification is a large black magnifier with a question mark, its outcomes marked by a red circled cross (Refine Program) and a green circled check (Add New Skill). Dotted blue leader lines tie lines of code to the item icons they use.
proposed_highlight: Each component is named in its coloured heading bar and its outgoing arrows share that colour, so a reader can follow which loop belongs to which component; the outcome of verification is carried by red-cross and green-check icons on the two outgoing arrows.
lesson: Give each agent component its own pastel heading bar and draw its arrows in a darker shade of that hue, then show the real artefacts in place (task screenshots on an arc, the generated code listing, an icon-per-row skill list) with a check or cross deciding which arrow fires.
notes: elements 'other' = the monospace code listing panel and the check/cross outcome glyphs. Venue written as arXiv: remembered as TMLR, but nothing read here confirms it (arXiv fallback, no venue line on the PDF first page); year = arXiv preprint year.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: the yellow Skill Library panel sits to the right of the central code panel, feeding retrieved skills leftward into the program and receiving verified new skills by an arrow from self-verification

relations.form: the automatic curriculum is a circular cycle of round Minecraft task screenshots (Mine Wood Log -> Make Crafting Table -> Combat Zombie -> Mine Diamond) joined by curved arrows, one dashed

the iterative prompting loop is a vertical pair of arrows between the code panel and the Minecraft environment screenshot (Code as Actions down, Env Feedback / Execution Errors up) plus a red Refine Program arrow up from Self-Verification
Skill Retrieval is a blue arrow from the library panel into the code panel, and the retrieved skills are drawn as item icons pinned by dotted lines to the code lines that call them
three titled columns left to right (Automatic Curriculum, Iterative Prompting Mechanism, Skill Library) with a purple New Task arrow from the curriculum into the code panel
the program is a real JavaScript snippet in a grey code panel, tasks are game screenshots, and skills are pixel-art item icons with names

channels.colour: header pill colour = module (purple curriculum, blue prompting, yellow library), and arrow/text colour matches the module that owns it (purple New Task and Update Exploration Progress, blue Skill Retrieval); red/green additionally mean fail/pass (Refine Program with an X, Add New Skill with a check), and green also marks the newly added skill in the library list
channels.shape: circles = tasks, grey code panel = program, magnifier icon = self-verification, item icons = skills
channels.line: solid arrows for control/data, one dashed curriculum arrow for a not-yet-reached task, dotted lines tie code lines to skill icons
channels.frame: only the skill library is enclosed in a yellow panel

quality.strengths: Every noun is real data (screenshots, an actual combatZombie program, item icons); the library-to-code retrieval and the verification-to-library addition are both drawn as short arrows with matching colours; the three columns match the three named components.
quality.weaknesses: Colour carries two meanings (module identity and pass/fail), and green is reused for the added skill text; the Update Exploration Progress and Add New Skill arrows run long L-shaped paths along the bottom, the latter across the whole right half to reach the library.

insights.structure: Three titled columns with coloured header pills: Automatic Curriculum (purple, a cycle of circular game screenshots), Iterative Prompting Mechanism (blue, a code panel above a Minecraft screenshot and a magnifier 'Self-Verification' icon), and Skill Library (yellow, a list of item icons with skill names).
insights.data: Tasks are circular Minecraft screenshots, the program is a real JavaScript snippet in a grey code panel with item icons pinned to called functions, and skills are pixel-art item icons beside names.
insights.emphasis: Arrow and text colours match the module they belong to: purple 'New Task' and 'Update Exploration Progress', blue 'Skill Retrieval', red 'Refine Program' with an X, green 'Add New Skill' with a check.
insights.flow: Curriculum feeds a new task rightward into the code panel, the library feeds skills leftward into it, code goes down to the environment and feedback up, and self-verification branches up (refine) or right to the library (add).
insights.avoid: The long thin coloured arrows along the bottom are faint and cross under icons, and skill names in the library change colour (blue/green/black) with no legend.

arrangement.units: three vertical columns each topped by a coloured header pill; only the skill library is enclosed in a yellow panel
arrangement.shared: the Minecraft environment and self-verification sit centrally under the prompting column and connect to all three
